title: Patients' Perceptions of the Ongoing Digitalization in General and Visceral Surgery
summary: General and visceral surgery increasingly use new digital technologies – above all surgical robots, but also programs based on artificial intelligence (AI). Many people are open to these technologies but at the same time have questions or concerns, for example about technical errors, the role of the doctor, or the protection of their personal data. This study aims to find out how patients think about such digital developments in surgery. To do so, patients complete a voluntary questionnaire during their first visit to the surgical outpatient clinic of University Hospital RWTH Aachen – before the doctor’s information and consent discussion takes place. The aim is to capture as broad a picture as possible of patients’ opinions, expectations and concerns. The findings should help to inform patients about these technologies more clearly and effectively in the future.
conditions: patients at elective first presentation in the general and visceral surgery outpatient clinic; oncological subsample for the AI module.

interventions.name:
The robotic-surgery questionnaire is the study's primary data-collection instrument. The intended completion time is about 10-15 minutes. The questionnaire covers several content areas:
•	sociodemographic data in broad categories,
•	previous surgical experience,
•	prior knowledge of robotic-assis

Patients with an oncological indication additionally receive the AI module. The intended completion time is about 10-12 minutes. The AI questionnaire covers:
•	sociodemographic data in broad categories,
•	planned surgical region,
•	previous use of AI applications,
•	subjective level of informati

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Planned elective presentation in the visceral surgery outpatient clinic (robotic-surgery questionnaire); for the AI questionnaire additionally an oncological indication
•	Sufficient German language skills; ability to answer independently
Exclusion criteria:
•	Lack of capacity to consent or relevant cognitive impairment
•	Insufficient language skills
